kurz: Pure starch thickens liquids and makes surfaces crisp. In the wrong place it makes things sticky.
bild_im_kopf: Like flour with everything else taken out: just the swelling granules, without protein that could make things tough.
was_passiert: Starch powder is nothing but starch granules. In warm water they swell and thicken. As a dry, thin layer in the oven they harden into a brittle crust. Potato starch thickens at a lower temperature and more clearly; cornflour has to boil and turns slightly cloudy.
faustregeln: Bring cornflour to the boil once.
For crisping, use only a dusting.

rolle.rolle: forms a crisp shell as a dusting
as a loose film makes things sticky and brown too early
